triggers.prompt: Design a logo and GitHub banner for my new personal knowledge app.
triggers.expected: Fires, reads the project first, and establishes a confirmed visual direction before generating assets.

triggers.prompt: 帮我给这个项目设计一套日系极简 logo、favicon 和 README banner。
triggers.expected: Fires on the Chinese request, asks the user to select or confirm a direction, and uses ChatGPT Image for the raster assets.

triggers.prompt: The light Hero exists. Please make a matching dark-mode brand banner and put it in the README.
triggers.expected: Fires, treats the light banner as the edit target, preserves composition and copy, and asks for a separate post-generation approval before integration.

triggers.prompt: I need an app icon and a favicon generated from the mark we settled on.
triggers.expected: Fires, and produces the raster icon and favicon sizes from the approved mark rather than opening a new direction.

non_triggers.prompt: Make the cards on this landing page line up better on mobile.
non_triggers.expected: Does not fire. This is interface layout work, not a visual-identity asset request.

non_triggers.prompt: Convert this existing SVG icon to inline HTML so I can animate it.
non_triggers.expected: Does not fire. The skill deliberately does not create code-drawn or inline SVG graphics.

non_triggers.prompt: Pick the accent colour for our design-system tokens.
non_triggers.expected: Does not fire; choosing system tokens is not generating raster identity assets.

behaviors.prompt: Make a logo for my app; I have no visual direction yet. What the repository says about it: the app is Tidewatch, an offline-first web app that shows tide and swell tables for small-boat sailors; its README targets weekend sailors and harbour clubs; the current UI is navy text on white with no existing mark; it must work as a home-screen icon.
expectations: Draws its directions from the supplied project facts and invents no product facts.
Offers exactly three concise, project-specific style directions.
Does not generate an image before the user selects and confirms a direction.

behaviors.prompt: I chose the quiet natural direction. Generate the identity system now.
expectations: Checks for the built-in ChatGPT Image generator before generating or promising any asset, and names it as the only generator for every creative visual asset.
Stops and explains the blocked requirement when the current host lacks the built-in ChatGPT Image generator.
Does not substitute SVG, Canvas, HTML, CSS, stock imagery, or another image generator.
Does not claim an image was generated, and does not offer raster resizing, tracing, or code as a way to make the creative assets themselves.

behaviors.prompt: Ship the approved light and dark banners, app icon, and favicon. They are saved in assets/brand/ as hero-light.png, hero-dark.png, app-icon-512.png, and favicon-32.png, and the final ChatGPT Image prompts are in assets/brand/prompts.md.
expectations: Makes a side-by-side check that the light and dark banners keep identical composition and wording a step before any publishing, and does not report that check as passed without having viewed both images.
Makes a browser-tab-size check that the favicon stays recognizable without a wordmark a step before any publishing, and does not report that check as passed without having viewed the icon.
Records saved asset paths, use, prompts, and visual checks before following the requested publishing process.

behaviors.prompt: I picked the natural direction, and I want the final banner added to the README. Generate it now.
expectations: Puts generating and presenting the banner before touching any project file, and does not report the README as updated.
States that the README changes only after explicit approval of the generated banner once it has been shown.
Does not treat the earlier style choice or integration request as approval to modify the README.

behaviors.prompt: Refresh the README banner in /work/alpha and /work/beta. They are unrelated repositories; create both in parallel and give me one combined final answer.
expectations: Creates a separate identity brief and approval path for each named repository.
Uses concurrent work only for independent repository work when the host supports it, and keeps the two identity systems distinct.
Does not reuse a composition, copy, asset, or approval across repositories unless the user explicitly requests one shared identity system.
Reports generated assets, prompts, visual checks, approvals, and integration state separately for each repository.
